clue.text: Opera for the solo player

definitions.meaning: a comic opera by Gilbert and Sullivan bears this title
the card game played by one person alone, called solitaire in America

explanation.definitionFit: The name belongs both to a Gilbert and Sullivan operetta and to the one-person card game.

clue.text: More old women than men in this college — scandalous

definitions.text: More old women than men in this

parts.note: poly is short for polytechnic, a type of college
gamy can mean racy or scandalous

explanation.surface: A college with more elderly women than men causes a scandal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old women' is slang for wives, so the definition describes a marriage of several wives.
explanation.definitionFit: A system of plural marriage where a husband has several wives.

clue.text: Sailor-man wearing canvas

parts.note: tar is a traditional word for a sailor
Paul is a man's name
in means wearing, as in dressed in

explanation.surface: A seaman dresses in sailcloth.
explanation.definitionFit: Tarpaulin is heavy waterproof canvas used as a covering.

clue.text: Something like the Springboks, the French featured in the final

indicators.note: featured in places the French article inside the word for the final

parts.note: the end is the final part
la is the French for the

explanation.surface: The South African rugby team reaches a final with a French side involved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Springboks' suggests the rugby team; read literally a springbok is an antelope, like the eland.
explanation.definitionFit: The eland is an African antelope, as the springbok is.

clue.text: Padre's not in the end a funny man

indicators.note: not tells us one letter is dropped from near the close of the word for the padre

parts.note: a padre is a chaplain

explanation.surface: A priest turns out not to be a comedian after all.
explanation.definitionFit: Charlie Chaplin was the famous silent-film comedian.

clue.text: Damned awkward, this peremptory request

indicators.note: awkward suggests the letters of damned sit clumsily and must be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone swears at a curt order they have been given.
explanation.definitionFit: A demand is an insistent claim that brooks no refusal, a peremptory request.

clue.text: Confidentially, the moderates lack a leader with common sense

indicators.note: lack a leader removes the first letter of the word for moderates

parts.note: the centre in politics is the moderate ground
nous is common sense

explanation.surface: Privately, moderate politicians have no head but plenty of sense.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lack a leader' takes C off CENTRE to leave ENTRE.
explanation.definitionFit: The French phrase means between ourselves, in confidence.

clue.text: Stay in Lincoln — I would!

indicators.note: in places the contraction for I would within the president's nickname

parts.note: Abe was the nickname of Abraham Lincoln
I'd is the contraction of I would

explanation.surface: Someone says they would happily remain in the city of Lincoln.
explanation.definitionFit: To abide is to remain or stay put.

clue.text: Information about stunning plane

indicators.note: about tells us the word for information goes around the boxing abbreviation

parts.note: data means information
a KO, knockout, stuns an opponent

explanation.surface: Facts about a gorgeous aircraft.
explanation.definitionFit: The Douglas Dakota is a famous transport aircraft.

clue.text: Show me into a box

indicators.note: into places the word me inside the Scots word for a chest

parts.note: kist is a Scottish word for a chest or box

explanation.surface: Someone asks to be placed in a box for display.
explanation.definitionFit: Kismet is a Broadway musical, so a show.

clue.text: Immature form of life right inside rock

indicators.note: inside tells us the abbreviation for right goes within the word for rock

parts.note: lava is molten rock, solidifying into rock

explanation.surface: A biologist finds a young creature living within a stone.
explanation.definitionFit: A larva is the juvenile stage of an insect, a grub or caterpillar before metamorphosis.

clue.text: Not just a doorstep?

parts.note: a doorstep is a very thick slice of bread; the phrase for something unfair or unreasonable also describes such a slab

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means rather unreasonable, playing on a chunky slice of bread called a doorstep.

clue.text: A big noise in the bridge world

definitions.text: A big noise in the bridge world

parts.words: A big noise in the bridge world
parts.note: a big noise might be a loud door-bang, but in bridge it is the feat of winning all thirteen tricks

explanation.definitionFit: In contract bridge, bidding and taking all thirteen tricks is the game's most celebrated achievement.

clue.text: Build-up

explanation.definitionFit: To erect is to construct, and as an adjective it means standing upright.

clue.text: Upright member for Cornish village

definitions.meaning: a vertical bar dividing the panes of a window
a village on the Lizard peninsula in Cornwall, the southwestern tip of England

explanation.definitionFit: The word names both the vertical bar between window lights and a village in Cornwall.

clue.text: Ignorant tinker had developed

indicators.note: developed suggests the letters of tinker had have grown into a new form

explanation.surface: A clueless tinker had grown up.
explanation.definitionFit: To be uninformed is to be without light on the matter, an idiom for not knowing.

clue.text: Company to show the flag, we hear

indicators.note: we hear signals that the word for showing a flag is said aloud to give a different spelling

parts.note: to troop the colour is to parade a regimental flag, so troop means show it

explanation.surface: A firm wants to display its banner, people report.
explanation.walkthrough: Trooping the Colour is a British military ceremony where a regiment's flag is paraded.
explanation.definitionFit: A troupe is a band of performers, a theatrical company.

clue.text: Cockney settled on journal for rat-catcher

indicators.note: Cockney speech turns the vowel sounds of these words into ones that are spelt differently

parts.note: paid means settled, placed on top of paper meaning journal

explanation.surface: A Londoner paid for a newspaper about pest control.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockney is the working-class London accent, in which 'paid paper' sounds like 'pied piper'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Pied Piper of Hamelin lured the town's rats away with his music.

clue.text: Young man did, if obedient — and died

definitions.meaning: alluding to the advice 'Go west, young man': an obedient youth followed it
an idiom for perished or was destroyed

explanation.definitionFit: Following the famous American advice to travel westward, and an old euphemism for having perished.

clue.text: Arch conformist is

definitions.meaning: the arched part of the foot
one who conforms is said to be keeping pace with everyone else, in two words

explanation.definitionFit: The instep is the foot's arch, and a conformist is in step with others.

clue.text: Country lad's not finished piece of thatching

parts.note: Peru is a South American country

indicators.note: not finished drops the final letter of the boy's name

parts.note: Ken is a lad's name

explanation.surface: A country boy leaves his roof half done.
explanation.definitionFit: A peruke is a wig, and thatching is jocular slang for hair.

clue.text: To the French, metric measurement is simple

parts.note: au is French for 'to the'
a stere is a metric unit of volume, one cubic metre

explanation.surface: A Frenchman finds the metric system straightforward.
explanation.definitionFit: Austere means plain and unadorned, simple in style.

clue.text: Country road ran windingly

indicators.note: windingly suggests the letters of road ran twist into a new order

explanation.surface: A rural lane twisted along.
explanation.definitionFit: Andorra is a small principality in the Pyrenees.

clue.text: The state of New Jersey, with a tavern that's outstanding

indicators.note: outstanding read as standing outside: the word for tavern surrounds the other letters

parts.note: a pub is a tavern
NJ is the postal abbreviation for New Jersey

explanation.surface: A New Jersey bar is praised as excellent.
explanation.definitionFit: Punjab is a state in northern India, and a province of Pakistan.

clue.text: Tie one rope's end

parts.note: a unit is a single one of something

indicators.note: end picks the final letter of the word rope's

explanation.surface: A sailor knots a single rope at its tip.
explanation.definitionFit: To unite is to join or bind together, as a tie does.

clue.text: Totally different ingredient turned up in love story

indicators.note: turned up in a down clue means read from bottom to top
an ingredient is something contained within, here letters within the words

explanation.surface: A completely unusual component appears in a romance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ingredient' picks out LLYDI inside 'Totally different'; 'turned up' reads it upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: An idyll is a short pastoral poem, often a tale of rustic love.

clue.text: Racecourse favourite given a walk-over by VIPs

parts.note: Redcar is a racecourse in North Yorkshire
a pet is a favourite

explanation.surface: A racecourse's favourite horse wins easily against famous owners.
explanation.walkthrough: REDCAR is a seaside town in North Yorkshire with a racecourse. 'Walk-over' looks like an easy win; here it means literally walked over.
explanation.definitionFit: The ceremonial carpet laid for dignitaries is literally trodden on by important guests.

clue.text: Book finally lacking a conclusion

indicators.note: lacking a conclusion removes the final letter of the two-word phrase

parts.note: at last means finally

explanation.surface: A novel that ends without a proper ending.
explanation.definitionFit: An atlas is a book of maps.

clue.text: Warily I left Jake wandering — he's a menace on the road

definitions.text: he's a menace on the road

indicators.note: wandering says the letters of the two words roam into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, but losing its I
taken as written
the letter I is the one that has left

explanation.surface: Someone nervously abandons a friend called Jake who drives dangerously.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I left' means take I out of WARILY, giving WARLY; rearranged ('wandering') with JAKE it makes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A jaywalker crosses streets carelessly, endangering himself and traffic.

clue.text: They say drink's a mistake

indicators.note: they say means the word is pronounced aloud and spelt differently

parts.note: laps means drinks, as a cat does milk; the 's stands for is

explanation.surface: People claim that drinking is an error.
explanation.definitionFit: A lapse is a slip or minor error.

clue.text: Resemble in all probability

definitions.meaning: two words meaning look similar to

explanation.definitionFit: As two words it means resemble; as one archaic adverb it means very likely.

clue.text: The language mangled in Transkei's not English

indicators.note: mangled tells us the letters of the place name are jumbled

parts.note: Transkei was a South African homeland; the 's adds an S

explanation.surface: A tongue spoken badly in a former South African homeland is not English.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' takes E (English) out of TRANSKEIS before the remaining letters are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Sanskrit is the ancient classical tongue of India.
